stemBlocks.value: Make l the subject of the formula A = lw.
Think first: l is simply multiplied by w, so one inverse operation will free it.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p055-q08 from workbook page 55.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide both sides by w so that l stands alone.

whyThisWorks.value: Division undoes multiplication. Because l and w are multiplied, dividing the whole equation by w cancels w on the right and leaves l by itself. The area relationship is unchanged; you have simply chosen to read the formula as 'length in terms of area and width'.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing l = A - w, treating multiplication as if it were addition.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing l = A - w, treating multiplication as if it were addition.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing only one side of the equation by w.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing only one side of the equation by w.

examTip.value: Ask yourself what is being done to the letter you want, then do the opposite to both sides.
